To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epigenetic inactivations of the IFN-regulated gene network play critical roles in the immortalization of LFS cells and that the reactivation of this gene network can induce cellular senescences.

IFN pathway is epigenetically silenced in immortal Li-Frumanii fibroblasts, but the reactivation of the IRF5 or IRF7 genes can inhibit cell proliferation and induce senescencelike phenotype in immortalized cells.

IFN-regulated transcription factor genes IRF5 and 7 are epigenetically silenced in immortal Li-Frumaneni fibroblasts, and the over-expression of either of the two transcription factors induces a senescent phenotype in the cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of epigenetic silencers of IFN pathway genes in the development of cancer and the reactivation and therapeutic implications of these pathways.

the epigenetic silences of IFN pathway genes and the role of IFN-regulatory transcription factor IRF5 and its family member IRF7 in cellular immortalization and senescence in LFS fibroblasts and in other immortal cells.
the role of IFN signaling in cellular immortalization and senescence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IRF5 and IFN-alpha can inhibit cell proliferation in immortal Li-Faumeni fibroblast cells and induce a senescent phenotype.
IRF5 and 7 can inhibit the growth of LFS fibroblasts, but that the mechanism is still unknown.
IRF5/7 can act alone or in tandem, in a dose-dependent manner, to activate IFN-regulated gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFN pathway genes are down-regulated during immortalization and reactivated during senescence.

the IFN pathway is epigenetically inactivated in immortal LFS fibroblasts, and that the restoration of IFN-regulatory factors, IRF5 and 7, can inhibit the growth and induce senescent-like phenotype of these cells.

epigenetic inactivations of IRF5/7 genes and their downstream IFN-regulated pathways are involved in the immortalization of LFS fibroblasts and that the reactivation of these pathways by the overexpression of IRF7 or IRF5 is sufficient to induce a senescent phenotype in the immortal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epigenetic silencence of IFN pathway genes is a critical step in cellular immortalization.
epigenetic silences of the IFN-regulatory pathway genes is a common event in immortalization of human cells.
IFN-regulated transcription factors IRF7 and IRF5 can act as tumor suppressor genes in immortal LFS fibroblasts, and their activation can induce cellular senescenece.
